name: South Carolina
overview: In South Carolina each county's official in charge of collecting delinquent taxes (usually the Delinquent Tax Collector or Treasurer) sells tax-delinquent real estate at a public auction at the courthouse or another convenient place in the county, after advertising it under the heading "Delinquent Tax Sale"; most counties hold one sale a year in the fall. The winning bid must be paid in full on the day of the sale by cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order. The owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor, may redeem the property within twelve months from the date of the sale by paying the taxes, costs and interest on the bid amount of 3% in the first three months, 6% in months four to six, 9% in months seven to nine and 12% in the last three months, capped at the amount of the bid. If the property is not redeemed, the official makes a tax title to the purchaser.

counties.how_to_bid: Pre-register with the county's Bidder Registration Form (for 2026 the forms were due Friday, October 2); registration is not offered on sale day, and there is a $10.00 registration fee per bidder. Pick up a paddle in Room 107 of the Delinquent Tax Office from 8:30 AM; the sale begins at 10:00 AM on the first floor of the parking garage at the County Complex. Bids are in person only (no mail bids), by the bidder or an authorized agent. The winning bid must be paid in full the day of the sale in cash, postal money order, cashier's check or certified check (no personal checks); a defaulting bidder can be fined $500 and barred from future sales. Owners have one year and a day to redeem, and the buyer receives a tax deed.

counties.how_to_bid: Only registered bidders may take part. Register free of charge, online or in person at the Delinquent Tax Office, during the week before the sale; a valid photo ID is required. Properties are auctioned in alphabetical order to the highest bidder. Pay in full by 4:00 PM on the day of the sale with cash, money order or certified funds (no personal or company checks); a bidder who does not pay is in default and liable for $500 per parcel. The defaulting taxpayer, a grantee or a mortgage or judgment creditor has one year from the sale to redeem; on redemption the bidder is refunded the bid plus interest of 3% to 12% depending on the quarter.
